name: enumerateDevices (camera, mic, speakers count)
plain: Lists the kinds and counts of cameras, microphones and speakers (labels only after permission).
meaning: Counts of cameras and microphones separate laptops from desktops and show headset use. Without permission labels and IDs are empty.

limits.headline: Can count your cameras, microphones and speakers, but names stay hidden until you allow
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, like a video call lobby.
can: Count how many cameras, microphones and speakers you have
Tell which kinds of devices are plugged in
Show device names once you allow camera or microphone access
cannot: See device names before you allow camera or microphone access
Turn on your camera or microphone by itself
See other gadgets such as printers or USB devices
limits.reach_label: A count, names after you allow

story.what_it_is: A page can list how many cameras, mics and speakers you have.

marketing.name: MediaDevices.enumerateDevices()
marketing.pitch: MDN says it returns a list of connected media inputs and outputs, with names hidden until permission.

story.for_you: You never see it. A call app uses it to show a list of your mics and cameras. A page can also see how many you have without asking.
story.for_makers: Makers need it to offer 'pick your camera' menus. Fraud and tracking tools use the count as one more detail that sets your device apart.

use_cases.example: A call app shows a menu of your microphones and cameras.
A browser game checks if you have a mic before offering voice chat.
A streaming site lists your webcams so you pick one.
A fraud tool sees that a visitor has no camera or mic, typical of a bot server.
An online exam tool checks that a camera and mic exist.
An ad system adds device counts to its fingerprint of you.

technical_bounds: No labels without a media permission
IDs reset when site data is cleared
